items.title: Resolve requirements-file find-links relative to the file
items.reason: The exact historical fix: it resolves existing relative `--find-links` paths against the containing requirements file and adds `uv pip install -r` integration coverage.

items.title: Change relative path behaviors for `requirements` files
items.reason: The broader requirements-file relative-path design tracker referenced by astral-sh/uv#20832. It does not specifically track this reported regression.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests using the exact error, `--find-links`, requirements files, both pip commands, relative/containing-file path semantics, local directories, file URLs, and the 0.12 release range. Inspected the strongest issue/PR chains. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#7113 and astral-sh/uv#9681 because their directories were missing; astral-sh/uv#8057 because it concerned argument splitting for paths containing spaces; astral-sh/uv#14367 because it concerned remote URL normalization and redirects; and astral-sh/uv#20786 because it concerned local HTML files.

type_reason: The behavior was intentionally implemented by astral-sh/uv#20832 and released in 0.12.1, so its return would be a regression. No open issue or pull request tracks that regression, making this a bug rather than a duplicate. The official Linux 0.12.3 binary did not reproduce the failure, so the macOS-specific trigger remains unconfirmed.
summary: astral-sh/uv#20832 is the exact historical fix, with astral-sh/uv#13239 as its broader design tracker. No open duplicate was found, and nearby same-error reports have different triggers.
draft_response: Thanks for the report. astral-sh/uv#20832 is intended to cover this exact case and includes `uv pip install -r` coverage for a relative `--find-links` directory. I also tried the minimal `uv pip compile` example with the published 0.12.3 Linux binary; both the equals and whitespace forms continued past URL parsing. Since your macOS result differs, could you rerun the example in a fresh temporary directory and include `uv --version --verbose`, `pwd`, `ls -ld requirements.in private_wheels`, and `python -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(repr(Path("requirements.in").read_text())); print(Path("private_wheels").resolve(), Path("private_wheels").exists())'`? That should reveal whether this is platform-specific or depends on an unrecorded path/input detail.
